$comment:
Tools are equipment, not commodities: they are owned as individual pieces, they wear out, and they gate which recipes a worker may perform. They can still be bought, sold and stolen.

`baseWear` is the most wear a tool will take, and it is ON THE BOARD'S SCALE now. It was `baseDurability` and it ran from 14 to 34, counted on the tool itself, because there was no track for it - and the reason there was no track was that a number running past twenty will not stand on a fourteen-rung ladder. There is a track now, four of them, one beside each kit slot on the player board (data/playerboard.json), so the number came down to meet the board rather than the board going up to meet the number - the same trade the kilogram made when a hero could not stand their own load on it.

Nothing got shorter, because the clock changed with the scale: wear was one point a LABOUR HOUR and is one point a JOB (rules.json wear). An axe was 24 wear at 3 hours a job, which is eight jobs; it is 10 wear at one a job, which is ten. Slightly longer-lived, and nobody adds hours up any more.

A tool is not the only thing that wears any more either. Everything a figure carries does - see data/items.json - and this file is simply where the first things that did are kept.

tools.name: Axe
tools.summary: Fells trees standing on forest tiles.
tools.story: The first tool a settlement buys and the last one it will let go. Forest into lumber, and lumber into everything else there is.

tools.name: Saw
tools.summary: Turns logs into lumber at a sawmill.
tools.story: An axe takes the tree down; a saw decides what it becomes. The teeth are the expensive part and the reason it sleeps indoors.

tools.name: Pick
tools.summary: Breaks rock. Required for coal, ore and stone.
tools.story: Everything under the hills comes up through the eye of one of these. Miners name theirs, which tells you most of what you need to know about mining.

tools.name: Shovel
tools.summary: Moves loose ground: clay, sand, peat, earthworks.

tools.name: Hammer
tools.summary: The general construction tool, and the smith's own tool.
tools.story: The tool that makes the tools. A smithy is a fire, an anvil and this, and the first two can be borrowed.

tools.name: Shears
tools.summary: Takes fleece off a sheep without taking the sheep off the board.

tools.name: Scythe
tools.story: Set the nibs to the man, never the man to the snaith. A harvest is won in the fitting and lost in the sharpening.
tools.optionalNote: Harvesting is possible bare-handed; a scythe doubles the yield.

tools.name: Plough
tools.summary: Breaks ground for sowing. A draught animal doubles its output.
tools.optionalNote: Sowing is possible bare-handed; a plough halves the hours.

tools.name: Fishing Net
tools.summary: Worked from a dock or a boat on a water tile.

tools.name: Loom
tools.summary: Yarn into cloth. Bulky enough that it lives inside a weaver's shed.

tools.name: Surveyor's Kit
tools.summary: Carried by a prospector. Turns a hunch into a marked deposit.

tools.name: Alembic
tools.summary: Glass still for brewing potions at an alchemist's.
